content: Golimumab may increase your susceptibility to infections or exacerbate existing infections. Avoid close contact with individuals who have contagious infections, such as chickenpox, COVID-19, measles, or the flu. Inform your healthcare provider that you are using golimumab before receiving any immunizations or vaccinations. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used if absolutely necessary. Discuss the potential risks and benefits with your doctor. It is not known whether this drug passes into breast milk. Drug interactions can alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. Maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription drugs, over-the-counter medications, and herbal supplements, and share this information with your doctor and pharmacist. In the event of an overdose with severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. While using this medication, regular laboratory and medical tests, such as complete blood counts, liver function tests, and skin examinations, should be conducted. Ensure you attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. This medication has been prescribed specifically for your current condition. Do not use it for another condition unless directed by your doctor. Store golimumab in the refrigerator and do not freeze it. Keep it in its original carton to protect it from light. If necessary, it may be stored at room temperature, but once stored at room temperature, do not return it to the refrigerator, and discard it after 30 days. Dispose of any unused portion after use. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Your medical condition may cause complications in a medical emergency. Always inform healthcare professionals about your condition. This medication is used to reduce pain and swelling associated with certain types of arthritis, such as rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, and ankylosing spondylitis. It works by blocking a protein in the immune system called tumor necrosis factor (TNF), which contributes to joint swelling and damage. By reducing joint swelling, golimumab helps prevent further joint damage and preserves joint function. It is also used to treat ulcerative colitis. Before using golimumab, read the Medication Guide and Instructions for Use provided by your pharmacist. Consult your healthcare professional on how to prepare and administer this medication. Inject it under the skin as directed by your doctor, usually once a month. The injection can be administered in the thigh, abdomen, or upper arm. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition. If you are using this medication for ulcerative colitis, your doctor may prescribe a different schedule or higher dose at the start of treatment. Allow the medication to reach room temperature by taking it out of the refrigerator at least 30 minutes before injection. Do not warm it using other methods, such as microwaving or placing it in hot water. Do not shake the medication. Inspect the product for cloudiness, large particles, or discoloration before use. If any of these are present, do not use the liquid. Before injecting each dose, clean the injection site with rubbing alcohol. Rotate the injection site each time to minimize skin injury. Avoid injecting into skin that is sore, bruised, red, scaly, or hard. To reduce bruising, do not rub the injection site after administering the shot. Use this medication regularly to achieve the maximum benefit. Redness, itching, pain, or swelling at the injection site may occur. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. If you experience side effects, contact your doctor for medical advice. In the U.S., you can also report side effects to the FDA. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. Before using golimumab, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients, such as natural rubber or latex, which can cause allergic reactions or other problems.
